segments.text: Review elimination, then reveal the whole roadmap: record its multipliers in L while the final upper-triangular matrix becomes U.
Work through a simple two-by-two example step by step, keeping the elimination multiplier visible.
Build L from the stored multipliers and U from the eliminated matrix. Multiply L and U to check that they reconstruct A.
Move to a harder three-by-three matrix and ask students to predict where each new multiplier belongs.
Contrast the factorization with repeated elimination: once A equals LU is available, many right-hand sides can reuse it.
Summarize the decomposition into two easier systems and transfer the method to a new right-hand side b.
